questions.question:
**Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, then select the option "No error".**

And it just recently awarded/ a million-dollar contract/ that reeks of corruption.
questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is **No error.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is** grammatically correct.**
 
• There is no error in any segment of the sentence. 
 
• The sentence is in the **simple past tense**, and all the words are used correctly in their respective places.
 
• The subject** "it"** is followed by the verb **"awarded" **in the past tense, and the object** "a million-dollar contract"** is placed correctly after the verb.
 
• The relative pronoun** "that"** is used correctly to introduce the subordinate clause **"that reeks of corruption."**
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is** option 4, "No error."**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9074044cf96dc1d09ca89eac99180c3d7440ade1b364d09d47931959bf693cc8.png] Confusion Points__**

 
• ​The use of "just" with "recently" is correct and commonly used in English.
 
• **The word "just" is an adverb that indicates a short time ago or a moment ago, while "recently" is an adverb that refers to a time in the near past. When used together, they emphasize the immediacy or freshness of an event or action.**
 
• Here's an example sentence: "I just recently finished reading that book."
 
 
• **In this sentence, the use of "just" emphasizes that the completion of reading the book occurred very recently.**

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

The need today is for both sides / to introspect and re-examine the issue carefully / and resolve it amicably.

options.text: to introspect and re-examine the issue carefully
The need today is for both sides

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'No error'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence there is no error.
 
• Let's see the construction of the sentence.
 
 
• *The subject of the sentence is **'the need' **and the verb of the sentence is **'is' **which is a linking verb. **'to introspect and re-examine' **are infinitive phrases remember that when the infinitive verbs are joined with the conjunction 'and' don't use 'to' with the latter verb.*
 
• **'*and resolve'*** is also an infinitive phrase in this particular sentence. It is not used as a main verb.
 
• *The usage of adverb 'carefully' is absolutely correct as it tell us that how we need to introspect and re-examine the issue i.e. carefully and amicably.*
 
 
 
• So the given sentence is an error-free sentence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9074044cf96dc1d09ca89eac99180c3d7440ade1b364d09d47931959bf693cc8.png] **Confusion Points__**

 
• **to introspect and re-examine** the issue carefully and **resolve **it amicably.
 
• introspect, re-examine and resolve are used here as infinitives. **To introspect, to re-examine **and **to resolve.**
 
• **Resolve** is not used here as a main verb.
 
• *when the infinitive verbs are joined with the conjunction 'and' don't use 'to' with the latter verb.*

questions.question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose ‘No error’.

The Event Horizon Telescope can help scientists analyse the shapes and behaviours of event horizons.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**No error**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The usage of '**analyse**' is correct as it refers to examining something in great detail. In this context, it is used appropriately to describe the action being performed by scientists on the event horizons.
 
• The terms '**shapes**' and 'behaviours of event horizons' are relevant scientific concepts when talking about the study of event horizons with the help of the Event Horizon Telescope. This adds to the correctness of the content as well as the grammatical structure.
 
• The sentence logically and coherently presents the information, making it free of error in context to spelling, grammar, and usage.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 3) "The Event Horizon Telescope can**" initiates the sentence appropriately, specifying the capability of the Event Horizon Telescope, and there is no error in this part.
 
• **Option 4) "help scientists analyse the shapes**" is correctly phrased, indicating assistance provided by the telescope in a scientific analysis, thus making this option error-free.
 
• **Option 1) "and behaviours of event horizons**." complements the earlier part of the sentence correctly, providing additional details on what aspects the scientists are analyzing, which is free from any error.
